requirements.text: When two runs claim an issue at the same moment, exactly one proceeds
After adding the label, a run re-reads the issue
If another run claimed it too, the run that claimed first wins
The later run marks its progress comment as not started
The later run exits without removing the label
Either the claim writes its holder record itself, synchronously, before it re-reads, or the tie-break uses something that exists at claim time (for example when the label was added).
Amend ADR-005: the first claim wins a tie, and how "first" is decided
The ADR-005 amendment names its enforcing tests inline
A run that releases its claim removes its holder record (its concurrent claim note), so a later run never counts it.
"First" is read from the times GitHub gives the holder records. Records with the same time are ordered by their id.
If GitHub's reply to posting the holder record has no time, the claim fails closed: the run removes its record and the label and does not proceed. The run's own clock is never used in its place.
Another run's record counts only inside a window before this run's record.
The window is its own setting, ZBUILD_CLAIM_RACE_WINDOW_S, with a plain default of 120 seconds; it is not worked out from another setting.
After posting its holder record, a run does not re-read the issue's labels. Reading the holder records back is the re-read.
One read of the holder records finds both the winner and the run's own record.
Two real claims run through a fake GitHub: a stand-in gh that keeps the comments and labels our code posts and gives them back when read. No test hand-writes a reply that holds our own holder record.
The tests cover the winner, when the two records have the same time and differ only by id.
The tests cover the loser keeping the label.
The tests cover a reply with no time, failing closed.
The tests cover claim, release, then claim again inside the window.
The tests cover the window setting and its default.
Never touch the real repo.
The coordinator's unit test runs on macOS as well as Linux: no GNU-only sed -i.
The PR states the accepted known limit: if each run reads the holder records back before the other run's record is visible, both proceed.
ADR: docs/adr/ADR-005-claim-coordinator.md
